---
title: "Resources"
subtitle: "Free books and guides for learning statistics with R"
---

## Getting started with R

- [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/){target="_blank"} by Hadley Wickham, Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel and Garrett Grolemund: data import, wrangling and visualisation with the `tidyverse`.
- [Learning Statistics with R](https://learningstatisticswithr.com/){target="_blank"} by Danielle Navarro: a gentle introduction to statistics and R, written with psychology students in mind.
- [Modern Statistics with R](https://modernstatisticswithr.com/){target="_blank"} by Måns Thulin: from data handling to more advanced models.

## Visualisation

- [Data Visualization: A Practical Introduction](https://socviz.co/){target="_blank"} by Kieran Healy: making clear, honest figures with `ggplot2`.

## Mixed models

- [GLMM FAQ](https://bbolker.github.io/mixedmodels-misc/glmmFAQ.html){target="_blank"} by Ben Bolker and colleagues: practical answers to common questions about fitting GLMMs in R.
- *Statistics for Linguists: An Introduction Using R* by Bodo Winter (Routledge, 2019): linear and mixed models explained very clearly, with examples from language research.
- *Linear Mixed Models for Longitudinal Data* by Geert Verbeke and Geert Molenberghs (Springer, 2000): the theory behind the sample session.

## Bayesian modelling

- [Statistical Rethinking](https://xcelab.net/rm/){target="_blank"} by Richard McElreath: a modern, causal introduction to Bayesian statistics, with free lecture videos.

## Reproducible workflows

- [Happy Git and GitHub for the useR](https://happygitwithr.com/){target="_blank"} by Jenny Bryan: version control for R users.
- [Quarto](https://quarto.org/){target="_blank"}: documentation for reproducible reports, slides, websites and manuscripts.
